title: Elastic KV shard orchestration for mixed tensor/pipeline GPU layouts
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: As models scale across tensor and pipeline parallel partitions, KV cache placement that assumes one-to-one mapping to worker ranks leads to uneven GPU memory utilization, higher spill rates, and throughput cliffs under continuous batching. Goal: Build an elastic shard orchestration layer that dynamically rebalances KV ownership across heterogeneous GPU topologies while preserving low-latency token generation and stable p99s.

Scope: prototype control-plane + runtime hooks to: (1) observe per-shard hotness and access patterns under continuous batching, (2) compute placement decisions that respect tensor/pipeline co-location constraints, (3) perform live shard split/merge and migration with minimal KV cache warm-up cost, (4) integrate spill-to-host and NVMe tiers and coordinated prefetch so early-batched requests do not stall during migration.

Design summary:
- Monitoring: lightweight per-shard counters (accesses, unique keys, reuse distance distribution) sampled on-rank and aggregated by the orchestration leader.
- Cost model: estimate per-shard memory footprint, expected token access frequency, migration cost (bytes * bandwidth + re-warm token penalty). Prefer migration only when projected end-to-end cost < expected savings over T horizon.
- Placement heuristics: soft-affinity for shards that overlap tensor-parallel slices to avoid cross-device all-reduce on KV fetch; pipeline-aware co-placement for pipeline-stage-local shards to minimize inter-stage sync during generation. Allow hot-key replication to up to 2 replicas for sub-1ms p99 preservation under bursty traffic.
- Migration protocol: two-phase handoff: (a) shadow-replication to target GPU + warm prefetch of most-recent top-K keys, (b) atomic ownership transfer of shard table and update of routing table, (c) grace window where requests read from both source and target to avoid misses. Eviction pointers maintained to avoid double-free.
- Continuous-batching interaction: scheduler tags batch windows with shard-version and prefetch hints; runtime performs KV prefetch into local caches when upcoming batches indicate access to remote shards. Batch coalescer limits cross-shard fanout to keep latency SLOs.
- Spill strategy: tiered spill with host DRAM as first tier for ephemeral overflow, NVMe as persistent spill for long-term cold slabs. Migration respects spill residency (do not migrate shards that are mostly NVMe-resident unless strong benefit).

Success criteria (measurable):
- Reduce occurrences of GPU OOM events due to KV imbalance by >=90% in mixed-parallel workloads.
- Improve median throughput under continuous batching by >=12% and improve p99 latency by <=10% degradation during migrations.
- Keep remote KV fetch rate (network/PCIe) within budget defined by current deployment SLOs.

Constraints and risks:
- Additional orchestration overhead and metadata traffic could compete with RPC bandwidth used by tensor/pipeline synchronization. We must cap metadata aggregation frequency.
- Migration warmup relies on accurate hot-key estimation — misestimates can cause regressions. Plan to run conservative thresholds in canary.

Rollout plan: prototype in runtime-1.20 canary cluster with 8-node heterogeneous GPU sets, run synthetic and real customer-like workloads. Start with read-only replication (no ownership transfer) to validate traffic patterns, then enable full migration behind feature flag.

Notes: keep the design modular so Dedicated and Private runtimes can opt into orchestration or use static placement policies.
acceptance_criteria: Leader-based orchestration collects per-shard metrics with <2% CPU overhead on runner hosts
Prototype migration protocol completes shadow-replication + ownership transfer within configured migration window (default 10s) without observable p99 spike >2x
End-to-end test harness reproduces imbalance scenario and shows >=90% reduction in GPU OOMs vs baseline static placement
Canary rollout configuration exists and is documented in Confluence with runbook and rollback steps
